description: Estimate movement time with Fitts's law (Shannon form: a + b * log2(distance / width + 1)) and decision time with the Hick-Hyman law (a + b * log2(choices + 1)). Pass `distance` and `width` for one target, `choices` for a choice set, and/or `layouts`: 2 or 3 layouts, each {name, targets: [{label, distance, width}], choices} to compare total time. Constants are configurable with `fitts_a`, `fitts_b`, `hick_a`, `hick_b` (milliseconds; defaults a=100, b=150 for pointing and a=200, b=150 for choice, typical illustrative values). These are models: the defaults are not measured on your users, so use results to compare layouts, not to predict seconds. Sources: Fitts 1954, MacKenzie's Shannon formulation, Hick 1952, Hyman 1953, as context in Cooper's About Face and Norman. Constants and laws are stated from general knowledge, not verified against the design library.

distance.description: Distance to target along the movement line, any consistent unit.

fitts_b.description: Fitts slope in ms per bit. Default 150.

hick_b.description: Hick slope in ms per bit. Default 150.

width.description: Target width along the movement line, same unit.

name: calc_fitts_hick
title: Fitts and Hick calculator
